voiceover: One God, eternally three persons. Is that a contradiction — or the truth Scripture teaches? Here is how the section makes the case. It starts where Israel starts — there is one God, and only one. Yet the New Testament gives to the Son and to the Spirit what belongs to God alone. Where the doctrine actually came from — and whether the earliest Christians already lived it. And whether it holds together — with answers to modalism, and to Muslims, Jehovah's Witnesses, and Mormons. Every one of these arguments gets a fully-cited deep-dive essay. Each claim is sourced, and the strongest objections are stated fairly, then answered. That is our standard — Checked Before Published. And you will not just read. On every essay an AI tutor answers your questions — ask it anything, or highlight a single sentence and ask about that exact line. Mastery mode lets you explain the argument back in your own words and have it graded. Daily practice brings the key points back just as you are about to forget them. There are pocket cards to share, and a Debate Arena to practise against an AI sceptic before the real conversation. Every essay comes in a plain-English version and a full deep dive, with read-aloud audio. The Trinity is beyond full comprehension, but it is not a contradiction. What this section makes the case for is that it is exactly where the evidence of Scripture points — and that it holds together. Start anywhere, and follow it where it leads.
